rubrics.criterion: Every signature that was accepting the fields of a result entry as separate required positional parameters is repaired so the entry crosses that boundary as one value: in match generation (percol/finder.py), in the model's result read-out and selection/mark re-shaping (percol/model.py), in the exit-path action dispatch and candidate-text extraction (percol/__init__.py), and in the view's line-painting helpers that spell the same fields under different names (percol/view.py).
rubrics.rationale: The result-row clump is the primary bundle of this instance; a repair that leaves any one of the four pipeline stages still threading the fields separately has not resolved the row relation the task describes.

rubrics.criterion: The matcher flags (case sensitivity, invert match, lazy finding) are configured through one home on the finder: bulk application, clone/carried propagation, and the interactive case-toggle commands all use that single configuration path, and a command that flips only one flag no longer re-states and forwards the whole flag set itself.
rubrics.rationale: The flag bunch is the second bundle of this instance and the part the prompt ties to the maintainer's 'adding a fourth flag' pain; keeping per-site parameter-threaded flag application would leave that pain in place.

rubrics.criterion: The result entry does not fall apart into its three loose fields at any stage boundary any more: no helper signature in the finder, model, view or action-dispatch path keeps taking the entry's line, match information and original position as separate parameters (the renamed view spelling counts as the same fields).
rubrics.rationale: This is the concrete residual failure mode of a partial repair: some boundaries get a proper row value while others still spell the fields out, which the prompt explicitly calls out as the unreadable state.

rubrics.criterion: No point where the matcher flag set moves still passes all flags as individual parameters: neither finder construction/cloning, nor the command that re-applies flags after a case-sensitivity change, nor any bulk application route reintroduced by the repair.
rubrics.rationale: Surviving flag-by-flag parameters at even one of the three movement sites keep the add-a-flag maintenance cost this task exists to remove.

rubrics.criterion: All call sites of the re-encapsulated data were carried along to the new interfaces: the finder loop's row production, the model's result read-out, current-selection extraction and mark-selection building, the exit-path dispatch loop over selected entries, the view's results-page loop, the clone path between finder classes, the two case-sensitivity commands, and the CLI function that applies command-line options to a fresh finder instance.
rubrics.rationale: This instance's clumps touch six production files; a repair that changes the type of the bundles without updating one of these callers leaves the tree broken or still field-threaded.

rubrics.criterion: The CLI wiring still applies --eager, --case-sensitive and --invert-match with their original negation semantics: lazy behavior from non-eager, case-insensitive behavior from non-case-sensitive, and invert behavior from --invert-match all reach the active finder through the repaired configuration path.
rubrics.rationale: The startup wiring carries two easy-to-miss double negations; it is an instance-specific caller that must be adapted without silent flag inversion.

rubrics.criterion: After re-encapsulation, the extra caller-state values that used to trail the row fields (whether an entry is the current selection, whether it is marked, the selection index among results, and facts like 'invert applies here') stay outside the row value, threaded only where they are consumed.
rubrics.rationale: The clump members took trailing extra parameters at three different sites; folding those extras into the row to simplify the repair would change what the row is and recreate the read-the-whole-pipeline problem.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not leave behind an added indirection whose only content is to receive the loose field parameters and re-send them: e.g. a forwarding helper that unpacks the entry only to call another helper with the same three fields, or a compatibility wrapper kept solely to serve an old call shape that no longer exists.
rubrics.rationale: This is the plausible half-repair for a clump: keep the field-level helper and bolt a bundled facade in front of it, which satisfies the type signature but keeps both designs alive.

rubrics.criterion: Helpers that were introduced only to accept or supply the loose field parameters are removed once their callers use the re-encapsulated interfaces: no dead helper for composing result entries from fields, extracting a single entry field, styling an entry from fields, or applying the flag set remains reachable or defined-but-unused.
rubrics.rationale: The injected state adds exactly such field-level helpers; leaving them in place after re-encapsulation is the specific cleanup obligation of this instance, not a generic style rule.

rubrics.criterion: The repaired tree carries no leftovers of the field-threading design: no comments or docstrings explaining how the fields are passed parameter by parameter, and no unused imports, module-level values, or obsolete attributes that existed only to support the loose-parameter helpers.
rubrics.rationale: Concrete residue specific to this change: the field-threaded design's explanatory comments and support values stop making sense once bundles have a home and signal an unfinished repair.

rubrics.criterion: Observed filtering behavior is unchanged: match ordering, the query split into sub-queries, case-insensitive matching by default and case-sensitive matching when toggled, invert matching with -v, and the empty-query case (every entry is shown) all behave exactly as before the repair.
rubrics.rationale: Re-encapsulating a row that is taken apart and reassembled at per-line hot spots in the finder loop and selection paths can easily flip an index, apply invert to the empty-query case, or reorder a condition — these observable filtering behaviors are the instance-specific regression surface.

rubrics.criterion: The external shape of matches and selections is preserved for their existing consumers: entries produced by matching keep the same field order (line, match information, original position) and selection entries keep the same field order (text, position among results, position in the original collection), including the mark-based selection flow where the middle field means the position among results.
rubrics.rationale: This instance deliberately re-uses one helper for two different row shapes whose middle fields differ; a repair that unifies them under one meaning silently changes which value lands in the second field of a marked selection.

rubrics.criterion: Matcher options remain settable and readable as plain instance attributes on finder instances after the repair, so direct assignments from rc files, the CLI startup path and the interactive commands keep working without going through the new configuration path.
rubrics.rationale: percol's public extension surface (rc.py files and option wiring) assigns these attributes directly; a repair that turns the flags into managed state behind accessors or a struct breaks that contract even if the test-visible flows still pass.

rubrics.criterion: Terminal presentation remains semantically unchanged: selected, marked and basic line styles are chosen by the same conditions, and matched keywords are repainted at the same positions and lengths as before for every entry.
rubrics.rationale: The clump in the view sits inside the style-choice and highlight-repainting logic; re-encapsulation happens where a wrong field mapping would misplace or drop highlights without failing the headless test flows.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not change evaluation strategy: lazy finding still defers match production (and non-eager runs still rely on it), finder result caching and the prefix reuse behavior still work, and nothing in the dispatch path evaluates matches earlier or more eagerly than before.
rubrics.rationale: percol's lazy generator design is load-bearing for interactive performance and its cache, and the configuration path repaired here is the same path that carries the lazy flag; silently making the pipeline eager is an instance-specific silent regression.
